name: Applied Computer Science
about: Making machines, computers and networks work together, from embedded systems to software, in a three-year programme taught in Delft's tech hub, preparing you for high-tech firms or a master's.

name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
about: Microchips, sustainable energy and intelligent hardware in a three-year Delft programme, with project work alongside semiconductor companies such as ASML.

name: European Studies
about: Business, politics and law of Europe combined with professional skills and a modern language (French, German or Spanish), plus an exchange abroad and an internship.

name: Industrial Design Engineering
about: Designing products by co-creating with users and stakeholders, following one design process across very different projects, from playground equipment to interactive museum exhibits.

name: International and European Law
about: International, European and private law taught in The Hague, the city of international courts, with practical legal skills such as case analysis and legal drafting from year 1. Awards a Bachelor of Laws.

name: International Business
about: How companies create value across borders: economics, marketing, finance, operations and supply chain, studied with classmates from 40+ countries and specialisations such as finance and accounting.

name: International Communication Management
about: Project-based training in international communication: media campaigns, reputation, conferences and influencing target groups, graduating with a portfolio of professional work. Runs in three years.

name: International Financial Management & Control
about: Accounting, risk management, strategy and decision-making applied to real companies, from pricing for a small brand to budgeting for a multinational.

name: International Public Policy and Leadership
about: How governments and NGOs tackle climate change, inequality and human rights, learned by writing policy briefs, running campaigns and organising your own global-issues conference in year 2.

name: Process & Food Technology
about: Chemical and food production processes studied in labs and a kitchen, from cheese-making and brewing in year 1 to sustainable, biobased products in projects set by industry.

name: Safety and Security Management Studies
about: Terrorism, crime, industrial hazards and hybrid threats: assessing risks and managing security, with an optional minor in intelligence collection and analysis.

name: Sport Studies | International Sport Management
about: How sport is managed and why it matters to society, with leadership training and the idea of sport as a driver of social change running through a three-year programme.

name: User Experience Design
about: Designing with technology around what people really need, beyond screens and apps, tackling questions such as liveable cities and a green future through hands-on experiments.

name: Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence
about: How intelligent systems work and how they relate to the human brain: programming, machine learning and deep learning, human-robot interaction and cognitive neuroscience, with labs for brain and behaviour and AI robotics.

name: Digital Culture and Society
about: Digital culture and media in a globalised world: online identities, communities and social media, with strong training in writing; students publish on the programme's own online magazine, Diggit.

name: Double Bachelor: International Business Administration and Economics
about: Two bachelor's degrees in four years: international business and economics integrated from the first semester to the thesis, combining strategy and management with economic modelling, econometrics and data analysis.

name: Economics
about: How choices by people, firms and governments shape the economy, studied with economic models and data applied to inequality, growth and climate change, in a small international programme with an optional semester abroad.

name: Econometrics and Operations Research
about: Mathematical and statistical models for real decisions in business, finance and the public sector, from hospital planning to product flows, with an Improving Society Lab running alongside the first year.

name: Entrepreneurship and Business Innovation
about: How new ideas become businesses: entrepreneurship and innovation with economics, finance, law and ethics, plus hands-on Entrepreneurship in Action projects every year.

name: Global Law
about: A full legal training (contract, tort, criminal, constitutional law) that looks beyond one legal system, comparing jurisdictions and tackling global problems such as digital technology and decolonisation. Awards an LLB.

name: Global Management of Social Issues
about: Societal problems such as poverty and migration approached from organisations: management, HR studies and sociology combined, with simulations like a humanitarian emergency response team.

name: Human Resource Studies: People Management
about: The human side of organisations: wellbeing, inclusion, team performance and strategic people management, through psychology, sociology, economics and management, with HR analytics and consulting skills.

name: International Business Administration
about: How international companies run and how culture shapes business: a broad base in economics, culture and leadership, with much training in writing, presenting and research among 50+ nationalities.

name: International Sociology
about: What makes societies differ and what connects them: migration, cultural difference, poverty and inequality, linked to policy, with a second-year choice between culture and social-risk specialisations.

name: Psychology
about: The mind and behaviour, with a flexible curriculum of nine majors, including economic, forensic and medical psychology, combined with a minor of your choice.

name: Theology
about: Faith and reason, ethics and meaning, and religion's role in society, taught in a small community; the Tilburg School of Catholic Theology can award canonical degrees recognised by the Holy See.

name: University College Tilburg: Liberal Arts and Sciences
about: A small interdisciplinary college where you design your own path through philosophy, law, sociology, psychology, neuroscience, politics and economics, then major in social sciences, cognitive neuroscience or law, politics and culture.

name: Applied Mathematics
about: Mathematics used to model real problems from industry and government, from image processing to supply chains, then calculated and solved; you learn to work with specialists from other fields.

name: Applied Physics
about: Light and sound, flow and heat, atoms and particles, studied to find nature's laws and turn them into technology, with an emphasis on applying physics in Eindhoven's high-tech setting.

name: Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences
about: How buildings, neighbourhoods and cities are designed, built and reshaped: architecture, urban design and building physics and technology in one mix of design studio and theory.

name: Automotive Technology
about: The car as one connected high-tech system: electronics, motion and control for hybrid, electric and self-driving vehicles. Formally a major of Electrical Engineering, and the degree is a BSc Electrical Engineering.

name: Chemical Engineering and Chemistry
about: Chemistry and process engineering for new materials, cleaner energy and medicines, in the English-taught track; the bilingual Scheikundige Technologie has the same courses and no selection.

name: Computer Science and Engineering
about: How to design, build and reason about software systems and web services, including proving programs correct and efficient with formal mathematical methods, with the user kept in view.

name: Data Science
about: Statistics, programming, data mining and business analytics plus the law and ethics of data, in a joint degree with Tilburg University taught in both Eindhoven and Tilburg. Apply through TU/e.

name: Electrical Engineering
about: Electricity and magnetism put to work in chips, motors and wireless energy, organised around three first-year themes such as the connected world, from photonic chips to wifi.

name: Industrial Design
about: Designing interactive products, systems and services that combine technology, data, users and aesthetics, learned mostly through design projects: smart homes, intelligent clothing, health and play.

name: Industrial Engineering
about: Business processes treated as systems to analyse, model and improve, from logistics and planning to human behaviour and data-driven decisions, through projects with industry partners.

name: Mechanical Engineering
about: Designing and building products, machines and production processes, drawing on maths, physics and chemistry, with much of the learning done in project teams.

name: Psychology & Technology
about: Psychology applied to technology: how people use and are affected by technology, and how to design new applications with that knowledge, through small-scale challenge-based projects.

name: Sustainable Innovation
about: How sustainable technology actually gets adopted: costs, risks, regulation and social acceptance, seen from the side of citizens, government and companies, in Dutch and international context.

name: Liberal Arts & Sciences
about: A liberal arts and sciences degree you design yourself across many fields, with professional development and community-engaged learning, in a small residential college in Middelburg.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences (University College Utrecht)
about: Build your own curriculum from courses in over 20 disciplines across the humanities, social and natural sciences, in classes of about 20 with continuous assessment, on a residential campus.

name: College of Pharmaceutical Sciences
about: An English-taught track of the Pharmacy bachelor focused on discovering and developing new drugs, from the drug target and active ingredient to testing safety in patients, in classes of up to 60.

name: Economics and Business Economics
about: Economics and business economics studied together and applied to real questions such as climate policy or affordable healthcare; almost half the programme is optional, so you can combine it with law, geography or data science.

name: English Language and Culture
about: Anglophone literatures, cultures and histories plus English linguistics, with polished language skills; from 2026 you can also take Celtic languages such as Irish and Welsh as an option.

name: Global Sustainability Science
about: Climate, energy, resources and nature studied from local to global scale, with natural and social science courses side by side, to understand sustainability problems and help solve them.

name: History
about: European history in a global perspective from antiquity to today, then a History track or an International Relations in Historical Perspective track from year 2.

name: Linguistics
about: How languages are built, processed in the brain and change over time, studied with experiments, logic and a little mathematics. Year 1 is in English; one later track is Dutch-taught.

name: Literary Studies
about: Literature compared across languages, periods and genres, from epic to fan fiction, and in relation to other arts and media, asking what makes a text literature and what it does in society.

name: Media and Culture
about: Digital media, data, film, television, theatre, dance and games studied in their history, theory and social context, with workshops in theatre, music, visual arts, film and photography.

name: Molecular and Biophysical Life Sciences
about: Life at the molecular and cellular level through biology, chemistry, physics and pharmaceutical science, with wet-lab work, computer practicals, programming and bioinformatics in the first 18 months.

name: Philosophy, Politics and Economics
about: Political and economic questions studied through philosophy, politics, economics and, unusually, history, in a small intensive programme that admits at most 75 students a year.

name: Actuarial Science
about: Mathematics, statistics and data science used to calculate and manage future risks such as fires, crises and bankruptcies and their financial impact, preparing you for insurance and beyond.

name: Ancient Studies
about: The art, literature, philosophy, history and mythology of Greek and Roman antiquity and its neighbours, studied broadly across place and time, with material culture alongside texts.

name: Archaeology
about: Past societies and why they matter today: materials, people and landscape, and how research is presented, with fieldwork internships in the Netherlands and the Mediterranean. Run with VU Amsterdam (ACASA).

name: Business Administration
about: Strategy, marketing, finance, management, international and digital business, with work on corporate social responsibility and the use of AI in business.

name: Business Analytics
about: Analytics, AI, machine learning, programming and data-centred management used to solve real business problems, in a programme built around data.

name: Computational Social Science
about: Social science and data combined to solve real social problems: from day one you work for real clients on climate, health, inequality and AI, and present your results.

name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
about: How people around the world live and make sense of their surroundings, studying culture, power and inequality around climate, technology and geopolitics, and doing your own fieldwork.

name: Econometrics and Data Science
about: Programming mathematical and statistical models, applying them to real data and explaining the results, for questions such as how firms can grow profits sustainably. Start in English or in Dutch.

name: Economics and Business Economics
about: A broad economics degree on the choices of people, firms and governments and their effects on society, combined with how companies are organised and run.

name: English Language and Culture
about: The literature, language and culture of the English-speaking world, taught entirely in English, tracing English from a language of Britain to a global one.

name: European Studies
about: Europe's shifting borders, languages, institutions, traditions and populations, studied in central Amsterdam with up to 300 first-year students.

name: Global Arts, Culture and Politics
about: Climate change, inequality and other big challenges seen through culture, politics and the arts, with four majors: human and artificial intelligence, curating the past, sustainability, or culture and social justice.

name: Global Communication Science (Communication Science)
about: How media and digital platforms shape what people see and believe across cultures, and why what goes viral in one country may be banned in another.

name: Human Geography and Planning
about: How cities, towns and neighbourhoods work and how policy shapes daily life, from affordable housing to climate impacts, learned in small groups through research and practical plans.

name: Linguistics
about: The structure, acquisition and diversity of the world's languages; in year 1 you also learn a new language and compare it with those you already speak.

name: Literary and Cultural Analysis (Literary Studies)
about: Literature alongside social media, art installations, political speeches and museums, analysed from an interdisciplinary angle to address the philosophical and social questions of our time.

name: Media and Culture
about: The global media landscape from animation and arthouse cinema to blockbusters, reality TV and AI-generated content, starting with a broad base in media history and theory.

name: Media and Information
about: Critical study of information technologies from social media platforms to AI, preparing you for work where technology, information and culture meet.

name: Political Science
about: Politics beyond governments and parties: how societies function and how to make an impact in communities and the world.

name: Politics, Psychology, Law and Economics (PPLE)
about: A small interdisciplinary college joining politics, psychology, law and economics to approach social problems from several angles and design new solutions.

name: Psychology
about: How the mind and behaviour work, to help people with challenges at work, as consumers or in mental health, in small groups with mentor meetings in years 1 and 2.

name: Sign Language Linguistics (Linguistics)
about: Sign languages from around the world: their structure, acquisition and use studied as a linguist, at one of the few universities with a full programme on visual-spatial languages.

name: Sociology
about: How societies work and how social rules and inequality shape lives, across education, work, gender, class, media and politics, with research skills to improve society.

name: Artificial Intelligence
about: AI designed to work with people (hybrid intelligence): machine learning and reasoning applied to healthcare robots, smarter triage, misinformation and sustainable energy, with attention to trust and responsibility.

name: Business Analytics
about: Mathematics, data analysis, computer science and business combined to turn data into decisions, from stock levels to seat pricing; the programme has run at VU for more than 35 years.

name: Communication and Information Studies
about: How communication works and what language does in it, from persuasion on social media to the words that trigger associations. Two English tracks: Language and Media, and Applied Linguistics.

name: Communication Science
about: A scientific approach to media and communication, from misinformation on social media to reputational damage, with a research project on a topic of your choice every semester.

name: Computer Science
about: Computer systems from top to bottom, from algorithms and AI to chips, networks and cybersecurity, learning to build software that is secure, scalable and correct from active researchers.

name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
about: How people live together and respond to change, from climate and migration to inequality and identity, studied from within through fieldwork and attention to culture, power and identity.

name: Econometrics and Data Science
about: Econometric models combined with machine learning and time-series methods to forecast and decide, from a bank predicting inflation to a supermarket planning fresh stock.

name: Econometrics and Operations Research
about: Quantitative tools for economic and operational decisions, such as how financial shocks spread between banks or how hospitals can best use beds and doctors.

name: Economics and Business Economics
about: How consumers, firms and governments behave in economic systems, from single purchases to global decisions, with questions such as how to stop a bank collapsing.

name: History and International Studies
about: The historical origins of today's global society, such as democracy, inequality and climate change, studied beyond Eurocentric perspectives and with attention to marginalised voices.

name: International Business Administration
about: Business in an international setting: marketing across cultures, corporate social responsibility and responsible finance, and working in diverse virtual teams.

name: Law in Society
about: A broad legal education (LLB) combined with social science research methods, applied to terrorism, corporate environmental damage, platform workers and asylum.

name: Literature and Society: English
about: Literature and culture in English linked to social and political questions past and present, alongside other storytelling such as film, TV series and comics.

name: Mathematics
about: A thorough foundation in pure and applied mathematics, from primes in cryptography to maths behind AI and animal skin patterns, with a data-driven or research-oriented path later on.

name: Media, Art, Design and Architecture
about: Images, objects and buildings studied together and in context, from Instagram as a museum to tiny houses, tracing their contested histories in a mediated, global world.

name: Philosophy
about: Fundamental questions about knowledge, reality and justice asked about current themes, building a critical perspective on science, religion and society. Choose the English track after applying.

name: Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE)
about: A small, intensive programme combining philosophy, politics and economics to tackle questions of fairness, democracy, economic crises and environmental policy.

name: Political Science: Global Politics
about: Politics at the global level: international power relations and how they affect different societies, for careers taking part in or critically following politics.

name: Psychology
about: Why people think, feel and behave as they do, and how brain, personality, genes, environment and relationships shape it, applied to health, work, media and sport.

name: Animal Sciences
about: The biology of animals, from pets to livestock and fish, and how their health, behaviour and welfare connect with people, food production and the environment, including sustainable livestock farming.

name: Data Science for Global Challenges
about: Data science and AI applied to climate change, health and food security, such as spotting deforestation in satellite images or tracking how diseases spread. Choose the English track.

name: Earth System Sciences
about: How soil, water and atmosphere interact, from groundwater flow to atmospheric turbulence, learned through fieldwork, lab work, simulations and data analysis, applied to floods, drought and climate. Formerly Soil, Water, Atmosphere.

name: Environmental Sciences
about: The relationship between people and the environment studied through natural, social and technological sciences together, in international teams working on climate and sustainability problems.

name: Food Technology
about: The science of making food: ingredients, processing, packaging, safety and quality, applied straight away to real products, with room to deepen or broaden as you find your interests.

name: International Land and Water Management
about: Drought, erosion and flooding tackled with natural science, social science and engineering, with cases from Peru to Thailand and a third-year internship and research project abroad.

name: Marine Sciences
about: The sea seen from nature, food and society: marine ecology alongside the ocean as a resource for the people who depend on it, working with engineers, biologists and policymakers.

name: Tourism (joint degree)
about: Tourism studied through social, economic and environmental science, asking how travel can become more sustainable; a joint degree of Wageningen University and Breda University of Applied Sciences.
